'''Gillian Patricia Bates''' (born 19 May 1956)<ref name=whoswho>{{Cite web|url=http://ukwhoswho.com/view/article/oupww/whoswho/U6775|title = Bates, Prof. Gillian Patricia, (Born 19 May 1956), Professor of Molecular Neuroscience, Huntington's Disease Centre, Department of Neurodegenerative Disease and UK Dementia Research Institute (Formerly Sobell Department of Motor Neuroscience and Movement Disorders), Queen Square Institute of Neurology (Formerly Institute of Neurology), University College London, since 2016}}</ref> is a British biologist. She is distinguished for her research into the molecular basis of [[Huntington's disease]] and in 1998 was awarded the [[GlaxoSmithKline Prize]] as a co-discoverer of the cause of this disease. As of 2016, she is Professor of Neurogenetics at [[UCL Institute of Neurology]] and the co-director of UCL Huntington's Disease Centre.<ref name="ucl-bates">{{cite web|title=Prof. G. Bates|url=http://www.ucl.ac.uk/ion/departments/sobell/Research/GBates|website=www.ucl.ac.uk|access-date=10 June 2016}}</ref><ref>{{Scopus|id=35380748900}}</ref>

==Education==
Bates was educated at [[Kenilworth School and Sixth Form|Kenilworth Grammar School]] and the [[University of Sheffield]] where she graduated with a [[Bachelor of Science]] degree in 1979.<ref name=whoswho/> She completed her postgraduate study at [[Birkbeck College, London]] where she was awarded a [[Master of Science]] degree in 1984 followed by  [[St Mary's Hospital Medical School]] where she was awarded a [[PhD]] in 1987 for [[genetic mapping]] of the [[cystic fibrosis]] gene, working in the lab of [[Robert Williamson (physician)|Robert Williamson]].<ref name=whoswho/><ref name=phd>{{cite thesis |degree=PhD |first=Gillian Patricia|last=Bates |title=Molecular approaches towards the fine genetic mapping of human chromosomes : with special reference to the cystic fibrosis gene |publisher=[[University of London]] |date=1987 |url=http://catalogue.libraries.london.ac.uk/record=b1533637 |oclc=940163599}}</ref>

==Research==
Bates's research has focused on [[Huntington's disease]]. She was one of the group who first cloned the [[Huntingtin|Huntington's disease gene]].<ref name="Macdonald1993">{{cite journal|last1=Macdonald|first1=M|title=A novel gene containing a trinucleotide repeat that is expanded and unstable on Huntington's disease chromosomes|journal=Cell|volume=72|issue=6|year=1993|pages=971–983|doi=10.1016/0092-8674(93)90585-E|pmid=8458085|hdl=2027.42/30901|s2cid=802885|url=https://deepblue.lib.umich.edu/bitstream/2027.42/30901/3/0000570.pdf|hdl-access=free}}</ref><ref name="MangiariniSathasivam1996">{{cite journal|last1=Mangiarini|first1=Laura|last2=Sathasivam|first2=Kirupa|last3=Seller|first3=Mary|last4=Cozens|first4=Barbara|last5=Harper|first5=Alex|last6=Hetherington|first6=Colin|last7=Lawton|first7=Martin|last8=Trottier|first8=Yvon|last9=Lehrach|first9=Hans|last10=Davies|first10=Stephen W|last11=Bates|first11=Gillian P|title=Exon 1 of the HD Gene with an Expanded CAG Repeat Is Sufficient to Cause a Progressive Neurological Phenotype in Transgenic Mice|journal=Cell|volume=87|issue=3|year=1996|pages=493–506|doi=10.1016/S0092-8674(00)81369-0|pmid=8898202|s2cid=9619253|doi-access=free}}</ref> She also created the first mouse model of the disease, the R6/2 mouse, an important step in understanding the pathogenesis of Huntington's.<ref name=RS_bio>[http://royalsociety.org/publication.asp?id=7705 Royal Society: New Fellows - 2007: Amos - Bruce](accessed 6 January 2009)  {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080609233936/http://royalsociety.org/publication.asp?id=7705 |date=June 9, 2008 }}</ref>

Prior to joining UCL in 2016, Bates was the head of the [[Neurogenetics]] Research Group at [[King's College London]].<ref name="kings-bates">{{cite web|title=King's College London - Gillian Bates|url=http://www.kcl.ac.uk/lsm/research/divisions/gmm/departments/mmg/researchgroups/bateslab/index.aspx|website=www.kcl.ac.uk|access-date=10 June 2016|archive-date=22 June 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160622180357/http://www.kcl.ac.uk/lsm/research/divisions/gmm/departments/mmg/researchgroups/bateslab/index.aspx|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Awards and honours==
Bates has been elected a fellow of the [[Academy of Medical Sciences]] (1999) and a member of the [[European Molecular Biology Organisation]] (2002).<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://people.embo.org/profile/gillian-bates|title = Find people in the EMBO Communities}}</ref><ref name=AMS_bio>[http://www.acmedsci.ac.uk/p59fid374.html Academy of Medical Sciences: Fellows: Professor Gillian Bates] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061001090615/http://www.acmedsci.ac.uk/p59fid374.html |date=2006-10-01 }} (accessed 6 January 2009)</ref><ref>[http://www.embo.org/communities/searchMembers.php EMBO: Search for an EMBO member] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090106012552/http://www.embo.org./communities/searchMembers.php |date=2009-01-06 }} (accessed 6 January 2009)</ref> She was elected a Fellow of the [[Royal Society]] in 2007 and to its Council in 2011.<ref name=RS_bio/><ref name=RSCouncil>{{cite web|title=Council of the Royal Society|url=http://royalsociety.org/about-us/governance/council/|access-date=5 November 2012|archive-date=16 March 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150316000007/http://royalsociety.org/about-us/governance/council/|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 1998, she was awarded the Royal Society Glaxo Wellcome Award jointly with Stephen Davies, for the "discovery of the cause of Huntington's Disease".<ref>[http://royalsociety.org/page.asp?id=1779 Royal Society: GlaxoSmithKline previous winners 2005 - 1980](accessed 6 January 2009)  {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080609053756/http://royalsociety.org/page.asp?id=1779 |date=June 9, 2008 }}</ref> In August 2024, Bates was recipient of the [[Royal Society]]'s prestigious Ferrier Medal, which recognised her work in understanding the molecular basis of [[Huntington's disease]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-11-30 |title=Ferrier Medal and Lecture {{!}} Royal Society |url=https://royalsociety.org/medals-and-prizes/ferrier-lecture/ |access-date=2024-09-06 |website=royalsociety.org |language=en}}</ref>
